name: HI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Ed Case running with $1.1M raised
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: Ed Case is an incumbent in a D+13 Honolulu district with a large fundraising edge over a challenger who has shown no financial support, and markets price his reelection around 96%. With no polls or expert ratings available, fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic win.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a competitive race or significant outside spending for Lam would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's 1st District is a solidly Democratic Honolulu-based seat, and incumbent Ed Case is seeking another term. He has raised about $1.1 million and holds roughly $600,000 on hand, while Republican Adriel Lam has reported no fundraising and little public profile. A Green and an independent candidate are also on the ballot but lack resources.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on the district's D+13 lean, incumbency, and the money gap. Prediction markets give Case roughly a 96% chance of winning, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating.
